name: Learning-Space Graphs Have Infinitely Many Contraction-Minimal Obstructions
statement: For every $d\ge3$, the truncated cube $\mathcal T_d$ and every distant two-vertex-deleted cube $\mathcal S_{d,t}$, $3\le t\le d$, are contraction-minimal nonlearning partial cubes. For every $d\ge4$ and $0\le r\le d$, the antipode-neighborhood-deleted cube $\mathcal U_{d,r}$ is also contraction-minimal nonlearning. Hence the contraction-minimal obstruction family for learning-space graphs is infinite and has unbounded isometric dimension.
proof: Each displayed set family is well graded. The rooted-union test excludes every possible root: translated missing sets contain a present partition witnessing failure of union closure. A contraction of $\mathcal T_d$ is a one-vertex-deleted cube; every contraction of $\mathcal S_{d,t}$ is a cube; and a contraction of $\mathcal U_{d,r}$ is either a cube or a one-vertex-deleted cube. These images are learning-space graphs, proving contraction-minimality.
